title: Population Data and Ecosystem Stability Review Test
description: Review practice for population data and ecosystem stability.

options: members of the same species living in the same area
all nonliving parts of an ecosystem
questions.correctAnswer: members of the same species living in the same area
questions.explanation: A population is one species in a defined area.

questions.prompt: A pond has limited nesting space. Which interaction may increase?
questions.questionText: A pond has limited nesting space. Which interaction may increase?

questions.prompt: Which data best shows a population trend?
questions.questionText: Which data best shows a population trend?
options: deer count each year for ten years
questions.correctAnswer: deer count each year for ten years
questions.explanation: Counts over time can show a trend.

questions.prompt: A food web shows grass -> rabbits -> foxes. If grass decreases after drought, what may happen first?
questions.questionText: A food web shows grass -> rabbits -> foxes. If grass decreases after drought, what may happen first?
options: rabbits may have less food available
questions.correctAnswer: rabbits may have less food available
questions.explanation: A producer decrease can reduce food for herbivores.

questions.prompt: A student says, "A population always grows if no predators are present." Which correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student says, "A population always grows if no predators are present." Which correction is best?
options: Food, water, space, disease, and other factors can also limit growth.
questions.correctAnswer: Food, water, space, disease, and other factors can also limit growth.
questions.explanation: Many factors can limit population size.

questions.prompt: A graph shows a population rising quickly, then leveling off. Which explanation is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: A graph shows a population rising quickly, then leveling off. Which explanation is most reasonable?
options: The graph proves resources are unlimited.
The population may be approaching a resource limit.
questions.correctAnswer: The population may be approaching a resource limit.
questions.explanation: Leveling off can suggest carrying capacity or resource limits.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows a ripple effect?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows a ripple effect?
options: plants -> no consumers -> no food web
drought -> fewer plants -> fewer insects -> fewer insect-eating birds
questions.correctAnswer: drought -> fewer plants -> fewer insects -> fewer insect-eating birds
questions.explanation: A change can ripple through connected populations.

questions.prompt: Which evidence supports that a predator affected a prey population?
questions.questionText: Which evidence supports that a predator affected a prey population?
options: The predator has a short name.
Prey numbers dropped after predator numbers increased, while food supply stayed similar.
questions.correctAnswer: Prey numbers dropped after predator numbers increased, while food supply stayed similar.
questions.explanation: A timing pattern with food controlled can support a predator effect.

questions.prompt: A lake receives extra nutrients, algae increases, oxygen drops, and fish decrease. Which factor directly stresses fish?
questions.questionText: A lake receives extra nutrients, algae increases, oxygen drops, and fish decrease. Which factor directly stresses fish?
questions.explanation: Fish need dissolved oxygen, so low oxygen can stress them.

questions.prompt: Which investigation best tests whether food limits a population?
questions.questionText: Which investigation best tests whether food limits a population?
options: Compare population growth in similar habitats with different food amounts.
Use habitats that differ in every possible way.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare population growth in similar habitats with different food amounts.
questions.explanation: A fair comparison changes food while keeping other factors similar.

questions.prompt: What does biodiversity often add to ecosystem stability?
questions.questionText: What does biodiversity often add to ecosystem stability?
options: alternative roles and resources when one population changes
questions.correctAnswer: alternative roles and resources when one population changes
questions.explanation: Diversity can provide backup interactions and resources.

questions.prompt: A student sees two populations rising together and claims one caused the other. What should they ask?
questions.questionText: A student sees two populations rising together and claims one caused the other. What should they ask?
options: Can the graph be printed larger?
Is there evidence of a direct interaction or another factor affecting both?
questions.correctAnswer: Is there evidence of a direct interaction or another factor affecting both?
questions.explanation: Correlation alone does not prove cause.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern could show predator-prey cycling?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern could show predator-prey cycling?
options: prey increases, predator increases later, prey decreases, predator decreases later
the graph has no axis labels
questions.correctAnswer: prey increases, predator increases later, prey decreases, predator decreases later
questions.explanation: Predator and prey populations can affect each other with time delays.

questions.prompt: A habitat corridor connects two separated forest patches. Which population effect might it support?
questions.questionText: A habitat corridor connects two separated forest patches. Which population effect might it support?
options: organisms can move between patches more easily
questions.correctAnswer: organisms can move between patches more easily
questions.explanation: Corridors can increase movement between habitat patches.

questions.prompt: Which model revision improves: pollution -> population decrease?
questions.questionText: Which model revision improves: pollution -> population decrease?
options: pollution -> water quality change -> lower survival or resources -> population decrease
pollution -> organisms choose to leave data
questions.correctAnswer: pollution -> water quality change -> lower survival or resources -> population decrease
questions.explanation: A stronger model names the mechanism connecting cause and effect.
